table_title: List the modern stock market crashes and bear markets from 1929 (Wall Street Crash) through the present whose Wikipedia master-list Notes column documents a clear proximate cause, with the year, the affected region or country, the cause category (one of: Speculative bubble, Real estate bubble, Sovereign debt crisis, Currency crisis, External shock, Margin/leverage failure), and a brief specific trigger description.
db_analog: SELECT crisis, year, affected_region, cause_category, specific_trigger FROM modern_financial_crises WHERE year BETWEEN 1929 AND 2025 AND notes_column_documents_clear_proximate_cause = TRUE ORDER BY year, crisis
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of stock market crashes and bear markets' master article, accessed 2026-05-13 (re-validated 2026-05-13 during cycle-1 / cycle-2 / cycle-3 repairs). Universe is the 27 stock market crashes and bear markets from 1929 (the Wall Street Crash) through 2025 (the most recent entry in the source) whose Notes column documents a clear proximate cause — the 'modern era' subset of the master article's 60-row chronological list, filtered first by Year ≥ 1929 and then by 'Notes column documents a clear cause' (which drops 10 of the year-filtered candidates whose Notes column is empty or describes only magnitude/timeline without identifying a cause: Kennedy Slide 1962, 1980s oil glut 1981, Souk Al-Manakh 1982, 1999 Greek crash, 2002 stock market downturn, 2010 flash crash, August 2011 fall, 2015-16 Chinese stock market crash, 2018 cryptocurrency crash, 2022 stock market decline). The dual filter anchors at the iconic Wall Street Crash and excludes pre-1929 events (Tulip mania 1637, South Sea Bubble 1720, Mississippi Bubble 1720, Bengal Bubble 1769, 23 'Panic of XXXX' 18th-19th-century events) which cluster heavily in 19th-century US/UK banking panics and add row count without much new causal variety. Per-row cells: Crisis name verbatim from the source's Name column; Year is the 4-digit start year of the crisis verbatim from the source's Date column (e.g., 'Bear Market of 1970' is staged as Year 1968 because the source's Date column shows 'Nov 1968' — the bear market started in 1968 and bottomed in 1970; the staged value follows the source's Date convention rather than the conventional Crisis name); Affected Region is taken from the source's Country column with normalization for clarity ('USA' → 'United States'; 'UK' → 'United Kingdom'; 'UAE' → 'United Arab Emirates'; multi-country Asia 1997 → 'Asia'; 'UK/Worldwide' / 'USA/Worldwide' → 'Worldwide' when impact was genuinely global; for the 2 rows currently in the universe where the source's Country column is NaN, Region is resolved from the Notes column context — 1997 Oct mini-crash 'Worldwide' from contagion language, 2001 September 11 attacks 'United States' as the attack target); Cause Category is a 6-value closed taxonomy curator-derived from the source's Notes column (Speculative bubble / Real estate bubble / Sovereign debt crisis / Currency crisis / External shock / Margin/leverage failure); Specific Trigger is a brief curator-summarized phrase from the source's Notes column describing the proximate triggering event. The 27-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon; future entries to the Wikipedia master list (e.g., a major 2026+ event) would extend the staged set; current entries are unlikely to be revised.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the `causal` near-saturation gap (causal at gap 2 before this staging; this instance brings it from 3/5 to 4/5 staged — gap 2 → 1). User-selected after a deep-dive on schema design for benchmark evaluation, picking the Schema B (5 cols: Crisis PK + Year + Affected Region + Cause Category + Specific Trigger) and Universe 'Modern era 1929-present' from 4 alternatives. The Schema B design prioritizes evaluability: Year is exact-match-numeric; Affected Region is exact-match from a fixed vocabulary; Cause Category is exact-match from a closed 6-value taxonomy; Specific Trigger is semantic-match free-text; Crisis is the PK lookup target. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 1 — the master 'List of stock market crashes and bear markets' Wikipedia article supplies all per-row cells via its 60-row chronological wikitable (filtered to Year ≥ 1929). Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited Wikipedia article HTML, (2) parse tables[0] (the 60-row chronological-crashes wikitable), (3) filter to Year ≥ 1929 by regex year-extraction from the Date column, (4) further filter to candidates whose Notes column contains a clearly-described proximate cause (drops 10 of the year-filtered candidates: Kennedy Slide 1962 'Also known as the Flash Crash of 1962' has no cause; 1980s oil glut 1981 / Souk Al-Manakh 1982 / 1999 Greek crash have NaN Notes; 2002 stock market downturn / 2010 flash crash / August 2011 fall / 2015-16 Chinese stock market crash / 2018 cryptocurrency crash / 2022 stock market decline have Notes describing timeline/magnitude without identifying a cause). Yields 27 events. (5) for each row, take Crisis name verbatim from the Name column, Year as the integer 4-digit year of the Date column (the source's annotated start year — e.g., Bear Market of 1970 is staged as Year 1968 per the source's 'Nov 1968' Date), Affected Region by normalizing the Country column ('USA' → 'United States'; 'UK' → 'United Kingdom'; etc.; NaN values resolved from Notes column context), Cause Category as one of 6 closed-taxonomy values derived from the Notes column's described triggering mechanism, Specific Trigger as a brief 1-line curator paraphrase of the Notes column's described trigger. Result: 27 rows × 5 columns, PK on Crisis, 0 duplicates. Cause Category distribution (27 rows after cycle-1, cycle-2, cycle-3 drops and re-categorizations): External shock 10 (1937, 1968 Bear Market, 1973 oil, 1980 monetary, 1990 Iraq, 2001 9/11, 2015-16 selloff, 2020 COVID, 2022 Russia-Ukraine, 2025 tariffs), Speculative bubble 5 (1971 Brazilian, 1997 Asian, 1997 Oct contagion, 2000 Dot-com, 2007 Chinese), Margin/leverage failure 4 (1929 Wall Street, 1987 Black Monday, 1989 Friday-the-13th, 1989 Rio), Real estate bubble 3 (1991 Japanese, 2008 subprime, 2024 China property), Sovereign debt crisis 3 (1998 Russian default, 2009 Dubai standstill, 2010 Euro/Greek), Currency crisis 2 (1992 Black Wednesday ERM, 2024 Tokyo yen-carry). Region distribution: United States 9, Worldwide 6, China 2, Brazil 2, Japan 2, Russia 2, single-country (UK, Asia regional, UAE, Europe) 4. Confidence gradient is real and strongly aligned with the `causal` category's intent (LLM tests cause-attribution): very-LLM-knowable causal-pair cells include the canonical crises (1929 Wall Street Crash, 1987 Black Monday, 2000 Dot-com, 2008 financial crisis, 2020 COVID); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-iconic crises (1992 Black Wednesday, 1997 Asian, 1998 Russian, 2010 Euro); harder calibration cells include the more obscure events (1971 Brazilian, 1989 Rio de Janeiro, 2009 Dubai standstill, 2024 China property, 2024 Tokyo yen-carry, 2025 tariffs); and the closed Cause Category taxonomy tests whether the LLM can correctly categorize each event into the 6-value vocabulary (the most challenging cases are events with multiple contributing causes that require selecting the dominant category — e.g., 1990 Early 1990s recession had both Iraq oil-shock and Fed monetary aspects but is staged as External shock per the Wikipedia Notes column's primary framing). Specific Trigger cells are 1-line curator paraphrases (8-15 words each) drawn from the source's Notes column; they preserve the proximate-cause specificity that the closed Cause Category abstracts away (e.g., 'Subprime mortgage collapse triggers global banking crisis' is more specific than just 'Real estate bubble').
